title: Audit Record
description: One append-only, immutable, tenant-scoped record of a governed act, resolving to exactly one Principal, or of a transition caused by an observed condition, carrying that cause and no Principal. A Policy Decision is a class of this record, not a neighbour of one
$comment: Normative prose: 40-governance/audit-model.md, properties A1 to A8, and ADR-0012. The retention period is DECIDED NOWHERE in this repository and no number appears here; no implementation can claim conformance to the term until it exists. Export is a stated requirement whose format, schema and transport nothing has designed; its completeness proof is ADR-0036's. Immutability is structural AND cryptographic: ADR-0036 makes every record of a Tenant a leaf of one append-only Merkle log in arrival order, with periodic signed checkpoints over it and inclusion and consistency proofs carried in exports. The log is over records rather than inside one, so no member here expresses it and nothing joins the write path. Where a member carries protected content — an Evidence Set, a Tool result, retrieved context or a Message — ADR-0037 has it encrypted under the Tenant's own data key before it reaches any store; identifiers, ordering and policy basis stay in plaintext.

tenant_id.$comment: A1 — the audit store is subject to the same forced row-level security policy, and the same CI control, as every other tenant-scoped table. An action affecting more than one Tenant MUST produce one record per Tenant affected: a record spanning Tenants could not be read under a tenant predicate without a bypass.

record_class.description: Which class this record belongs to. The class is a property of the record, not a runtime choice.
record_class.$comment: ADR-0013 splits the write by class. A policy_decision MUST be durable before the gated action is attempted, and if it cannot be written the action MUST NOT proceed. Every other record MAY degrade — buffered, retried, or written behind the action — and that permission is not an instruction: a record never written is a gap, not a saving. An implementation MUST NOT reclassify a Policy Decision as degradable under load. The cost is accepted in the open: the availability of the datastore an enforcing service commits to bounds the availability of every governed action it gates, and the audit store behind that service's outbox bounds only how current the trail reads (ADR-0034).

principal.description: Exactly one, and the one who acted. Present on every record of an act; absent exactly where the record carries a cause instead.

cause.description: The observed condition that caused what this record describes, where no Principal acted. A record carries a principal or a cause, never both.
cause.$comment: ADR-0030 and audit-model.md section 9. The schema requires one of the two and cannot forbid both without closing the object, which VERSIONING.md section 6 forbids, so the prose rule carries the rest. A Policy Decision always carries a principal (policy-model.md D2).

administrative_basis.description: For an administrative act, the administrative grant that permitted it, and the group membership it relied on where a group-to-role mapping supplied the role.

action.description: What happened, in Orchestra's own vocabulary.
action.$comment: A8 — the orchestration runtime's, a model provider's or the tool protocol's vocabulary MUST NOT appear in the audit surface, and a Checkpoint is never referenced (invariant I6).

entities.description: The entities the action touched, by identifier and by the values as they stood at the time.
entities.$comment: A5 — a record MUST stay readable and meaningful after the Agent, Workflow version, Tool, Policy, Model Binding or Principal it names is deleted. It holds identifiers and recorded values, never a foreign key a later deletion could null.

run_id.description: Present where the act belongs to a Run. Absent where it does not — an administrative act, for instance.

step_execution_id.description: The Step Execution gated, at a Step boundary.
step_execution_id.$comment: A Tool call inside an Agent Run has no Step Execution to key on. What the resulting Policy Decision references is an open question in the domain model, carried into policy-model.md E4 and section 9 — exact for Workflow Runs, unnamed rather than undefined for Agent Runs.

occurred_at.description: Wall-clock time. Informational for ordering purposes.

ordering_key.description: The deterministic ordering key for records within a Run.
ordering_key.$comment: A7 — wall-clock timestamps MUST NOT be the sole basis for order, because clocks skew across the components that write records. This key is INDEPENDENT of the event stream's seq, structurally and not stylistically: Audit Records exist for actions that belong to no Run and therefore have no seq, and A6 puts the record ahead of the gated action while the corresponding event is emitted after it. A record MAY carry the event's identifier as a correlation value; it MUST NOT use it as the ordering key.

event_id.description: Correlation only, where a corresponding Agent Event exists. Never the ordering key.

policy_basis.description: On what authority the act happened. Required, and required to be explicit when nothing applies.
policy_basis.$comment: A4 — where no Policy Decision applies the record MUST SAY SO rather than omit the field, since deny-by-default makes no-rule-matched a decision rather than a missing record.

evidence_set_ref.description: The Evidence Set this act rested on, where one exists.
evidence_set_ref.$comment: A4 names it as part of on-what-basis. Held by reference; the Approval Request carries the set itself.

inputs.description: The inputs the act rested on, recorded as values.
inputs.$comment: For a Policy Decision this is D2's inputs evaluated, and policy-model.md N3 requires any input outside N1's table — the evaluation time and the value read from a platform-defined aggregate (ADR-0035) — to be recorded here, or the decision is not reconstructible. D4 and D5: the same inputs MUST produce the same verdict, and reconstruction MUST NOT require re-evaluation. Replaying an old action against today's Policies may produce a different verdict; that is expected and is not a defect.

corrects.$comment: A2 — a record MUST NOT be updated or deleted within its retention period. A correction is a new record naming the one it corrects; the original stays readable, and both are returned by any query covering the period. Immutability MUST be structural, not conventional: the role that writes audit MUST NOT hold update or delete privilege on it.

external_reference.description: An opaque identifier minted by a rail, retained only so a customer can reconcile against their own provider-side records.
external_reference.$comment: A8 — permitted as an opaque value, and MUST NOT be typed, named or structured so as to expose the rail through a public contract. Under BYOK those provider-side records are the customer's own. Typed as a bare string for exactly that reason.

principal.$comment: A3 and invariant I2 — every record of an act MUST resolve to exactly one Principal and MUST carry the authenticated identity behind it, so attribution survives a rename or the Principal's deletion. Under delegation the record names the delegate who decided; the delegation grant is a separate audited fact with its own acting Principal. A record never carries an acted-for Principal alongside the acting one: should a delegation mechanism exist, the delegation is a separate audited grant this record references by identifier, and an acted-for member could be added later under VERSIONING R2 (audit-model.md A3). A transition caused by an observed condition — expiry, withdrawal, a wait elapsing, archival, a refusal no Principal caused — is not an act: its record carries cause and no principal, and MUST NOT name a Principal who did not act. Platform-operator work resolves to a platform_operator Principal of the Tenant it acts in (ADR-0030).

recorded_values.description: The values as they stood at the time, so the record survives deletion of the entity.

policy_decision_basis.description: This record IS the Policy Decision. Used with record_class policy_decision.
policy_decision_basis.$comment: D2 — a Policy Decision MUST carry the tenant, the Run, the enforcement point, the Principal, the verdict, the timestamp, the inputs evaluated, every Policy version that matched with the verdict each contributed OR the explicit fact that none did, and at a Step boundary the Step Execution it gates. Those first six live on the record itself; what is particular to the decision is here. P5 — it references the version and MUST NOT embed the rule text: an audit that resolves a decision against today's text reports a rule that may never have run.

policy_version.description: Deprecated by policy_versions, which names every Policy version that matched. A producer sets this member only when exactly one Policy version matched, and a consumer reads policy_versions.
policy_version.$comment: P4 as amended by ADR-0035 — a decision names every matching Policy version, which one member cannot carry. Kept rather than removed (VERSIONING R5), with its documented meaning narrowed while no producer or consumer exists.

policy_versions.description: Every Policy version whose rules matched, each with the verdict it contributed, each pair once and in no significant order. Absent exactly when matched_policy is false.
policy_versions.$comment: ADR-0035 — precedence is order-independent: any deny wins, otherwise any require_approval, otherwise allow, and no match is deny. Recording every matching version with its verdict lets a reader see why the verdict followed without evaluating anything again (D5).

matched_policy.description: Whether any Policy matched. False is a decision under deny-by-default, not a missing record.

gated_by_basis.description: This record is a governed act permitted or gated by a Policy Decision recorded elsewhere.

no_policy_basis.description: No Policy Decision applies to this act, stated explicitly rather than omitted.

policy_version_match.description: A Policy version that matched, and the verdict its matching rules contributed.

cause.description: An observed condition rather than an act: a deadline passing, a wait elapsing, the last pinned Run reaching a terminal state, a refusal no Principal caused, an invited administrator's first verified sign-in.
cause.$comment: ADR-0030 — the records a cause names are its evidence, never its actor. Attributing an expiry to the last approver, or to the author of the Policy that set the deadline, would be a false attribution.

condition.description: What was observed, in Orchestra's own vocabulary.

observed_on.description: The Audit Records the condition was observed on, by record_id: the raise of an expired Approval Request, the terminal transition of the last pinned Run.

administrative_basis.description: The role the acting Principal held for an administrative act, and how it held it: by an administrative grant to that Principal, or through a group-to-role mapping and a group membership.
administrative_basis.$comment: ADR-0032 — an administrative grant is one role from a closed set Orchestra defines, held in one Tenant and optionally narrowed to one Workspace. Checking one produces no Policy Decision (identity-and-access.md section 5), so policy_basis on such a record is none, and this member carries the basis audit-model.md A4 requires. Every audited act authorized through a mapping records the group membership observed at the check, because the directory that holds it is not Orchestra's.

workspace_id.description: The Workspace the role is narrowed to. Absent for a role held across the Tenant.

grant_id.description: The administrative grant to the acting Principal, where one supplied the role.

ends_at.description: When the administrative grant stops conferring the role, where it has an end time. A Platform Operator's always does (ADR-0030).

case_reference.description: The recorded support case or incident a Platform Operator's administrative grant names, held as an opaque value.

group_mapping_basis.description: The group-to-role mapping that supplied the role, and the group membership the check relied on.

group.description: The group as the identity provider identifies it, held as an opaque value.

observed_at.description: When the group membership was last known to hold, as the check saw it.
